featured_reviews.review_text:
Very divine environment. The temple is located in Kalbadevi. The temple is dedicated to Balaji. It is constructed in Tamil/ Dravidian style. Moreover, the temple has different sannidhi for devi. Every Saturday or maybe everyday morning, you will get pongal as prasad. Apart from this, you can buy laddoo. The laddoos are very good-yes, those big laddoos-similar to those served in Tirupati Balaji temple in Andhra Pradesh.

How to reach?
1. Get down at CST
2. Take a cab to Fanaswadi or take a bus and get down at Fanaswadi stop.

option 2:
1. Get down at Charni road station
2. The temple is 1kms from the station.

featured_reviews.name: omkar gurudu
featured_reviews.review_text: Sri Venkateswara Balaji Mandir in Mumbai was established in 1927, consecrated by Jagataguru Ananthacharya Swamiji, and is a replica of the Tirumala Venkateswara Temple. Its architecture is a beautiful example of Dravidian style, featuring an impressive Gopuram, a gold-plated Dhwajasthambam (flagstaff), and a Vimana over the sanctum. The temple is known as "Bombay's Little Tirupati" for its devotion to Lord Venkateswara and its observance of traditional Vaishnavite customs.

featured_reviews.review_text: Mumba Devi Temple is elegant temple dedicated to Mumba Devi, reflecting old Mumbai’s spiritual charm. The temple gets heavily crowded during Navratri, creating a vibrant and festive atmosphere. There are many prasad shops nearby, and pandas (priests) reside within the temple premises to assist devotees. Despite the rush, the place has a strong divine vibe and is a must-visit in South Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Paatliputraa Taekwondo Academy
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mumba Devi Temple is one of the most historically and spiritually important temples in Mumbai. Located in the bustling Bhuleshwar area, this temple is dedicated to Goddess Mumba, the city’s original presiding deity, from whom Mumbai derives its name. Visiting the temple feels like connecting directly with the roots and soul of the city.

🛕 Spiritual Significance
==========================
Goddess Mumba is revered as the protector of the city and its people. The temple carries a strong, grounded energy that reflects faith built over centuries. Unlike grand modern temples, Mumba Devi Temple feels raw and deeply traditional, making the experience more intimate and sincere.

🕰️ Darshan & Timings
===========================
1. Open: Daily (Entry Free)
2. Entry : Free
3. General timings: 6:30 AM - 8:55 PM
4. Aarti: Morning and evening aartis are conducted
5. Peak days: Tuesdays, Fridays, weekends, and Navratri
6. Early mornings are best if you prefer a quieter darshan.

🔔 Temple Experience & Management
=====================================
Despite being located in a very busy market area, the temple is well-organized. The queue system moves steadily, and devotees are guided efficiently. The surroundings are lively, but once inside, the atmosphere becomes focused and devotional.

📍 Best Time to Visit
======================
1. Early mornings: Peaceful and less crowded
2. Weekdays: Easier darshan
3. Festive days: Spiritually vibrant but very crowded

⚠️ Things to Keep in Mind
===========================
1. Dress modestly
2. Photography is restricted inside the sanctum
3. Keep belongings minimal
4. Be patient during peak hours

featured_reviews.review_text:
परनाम ! 🙏🙏        Jai Rajji!              Jai Shree Krishna!
Sri Krishna Pranami Mandir based on Pranami Sampradaya/Dharm - teachings of Mahamati Prannathji and Shri Devchandraji with their holy scripture as Shri Tartam Sagar.

History:
Shri Devchandra Ji Maharaj (1581–1655) was the founder of the Nijanand Sampradaya sect. Born in Amarkot, Sindh (present-day Pakistan), he displayed saintly qualities from a young age. At 16, he renounced worldly life and embarked on a quest for Brahma-gyana (divine knowledge), initially in Bhuj, Kutch, and later in Jamnagar.

Devchandraji dedicated himself to establishing a new religious movement, the Nijanand Sampradaya. This sect aimed to provide a distinct path to spiritual enlightenment. Devchandraji's teachings emphasized the realization of inner bliss (Nijanand) through the pursuit of divine knowledge and devotion.

Throughout his life, Devchandraji worked diligently to shape and develop the Nijanand Sampradaya, establishing a foundation for its followers. His teachings encompassed various aspects of spirituality, emphasizing the importance of self-realization and connection with the divine.

Shri Devchandra Ji Maharaj's contributions have left a lasting impact on the Nijanand Sampradaya, which continues to thrive as a distinct religious tradition dedicated to seeking inner bliss and spiritual enlightenment.

featured_reviews.name: Ashish Indani (Dr. Ashish Indani)
featured_reviews.review_text:
Among the important religious places of Mumbai and of Pushtimargiya vaishnav Sampradaya, Mota Mandir (the great shrine) has immense importance. The place is not only beautiful by its views, but also has excellent spiritual environment due to presence of shree giriraj ji and balkrishnalal ji under the auspicious residence and  service of many celestial  descentants of shree mahaprabhu ji.

Off late, this temple is caught in the controversy of ownership of authentic services of vallabh balak and self proclaimed services of trustees. By the principles of Pushtimarg, which is mainly meant for seva in the home, there is no concept of trustee or external and paid services. The temple is principally ownership of the goswamis. Vaishnavas are supposed to worship the deities in the temple by auspice of mercy of the goswamis. However, in the flow of changes when goswamis allowed a few sincere people to take part in management, and some greed of next generations of such external managers, the things started changing and some ugly examples like this have emerged. For visitors and pushtimarg followers, the right way is to follow the instructions of the goswami vallabh balak.

customer_updates.name: Champak Dedhia
customer_updates.text: यह फोटो मुंबई नगरी स्थित गोड़ीजी पार्श्वनाथ जिनालय के विविध प्रतिमाजी का है।गोड़ीजी पार्श्वनाथ स्वेताम्बर देरासर की प्रतिष्ठा ई. स.1812 में हुई है।यह मुंबई का दूसरा सबसे पुराना जैन मंदिर है।मुंबई का सबसे पुराना जैन मंदिर श्री शांतिनाथ जैन देरासर(फोर्ट) में है।गोड़ीजी पार्श्वनाथ का असल मंदिर सिंध प्रांत में था जो अभी पाकिस्तान में है।

featured_reviews.name: Vaibhav
featured_reviews.review_text: A 200 yrs old jain temple in the heart of Mumbai. In this hustle bustle area you will find peace and calmness inside this temple with beautiful white marble carvings and the antique lamps makes it a must visit place. There are total 3 floors.

featured_reviews.name: SACHIN THOKE - Visionary Man!
featured_reviews.review_text:
Shree Godiji Parshwanath Jain Derasar, Mumbai. Public sources identify it as a Śvetāmbara Jain temple dedicated to Parshwanath in the Pydhonie / Bhuleshwar area of Mumbai, with sources describing it as a historic temple dating back to the early 1800s.

A very peaceful and spiritually uplifting Jain temple in Mumbai. Shree Godiji Parshwanath Jain Derasar has a divine atmosphere, and every visit feels calm, sacred, and deeply blessed.
One of the most beautiful and serene Jain derasars in Mumbai. The temple is peaceful, well maintained, and filled with positive spiritual energy.
Had a wonderful darshan experience here. The atmosphere is pure, devotional, and perfect for prayer, silence, and inner peace.
A must-visit place for devotees and anyone seeking calmness. The temple’s sacred environment and peaceful surroundings make every visit memorable.
Such a beautiful and spiritually rich temple. The peaceful ambience and devotional feeling make this derasar a truly special place in the city.
Visited Shree Godiji Parshwanath Jain Derasar and felt truly blessed. The temple offers a deep sense of peace, devotion, and positivity.
A lovely derasar with a strong spiritual presence. The calm atmosphere and sacred surroundings make it ideal for quiet prayer and reflection.
Very peaceful, clean, and spiritually refreshing. This temple is a wonderful place for families, devotees, and visitors seeking blessings and serenity.
A sacred and historic Jain temple in Mumbai. Sources describe the Mumbai Godiji Parshwanath temple as an old and important Jain shrine, which adds to its spiritual charm and heritage value.
An amazing place for devotion and inner peace. Shree Godiji Parshwanath Jain Derasar leaves every visitor feeling calm, positive, and spiritually fulfilled.

featured_reviews.name: Keval Nagda
featured_reviews.review_text:
Extremely Poor Crowd Management at Varshi Tap (Tapsvi Parna) by Shree Godiji

I’m deeply saddened by the mismanagement at this religious event. The crowd is being handled terribly — people are crammed into enclosed areas and made to wait for hours in the unbearable heat.

Elderly people are struggling to climb stairs without any assistance. Despite the presence of so-called volunteers, there is no real help or support being provided.

This is not just uncomfortable, it's dangerous. One slip on those stairs could cause a stampede. It’s heartbreaking to witness such negligence during a spiritual occasion meant to offer peace and devotion.

If you're planning to attend, please think twice.

Sharing a few images to show the situation on the ground.

featured_reviews.name: Ojas Sawla
featured_reviews.review_text:
Divine Atmosphere between the hustle of city of Dreams not just seems unreal but give emance inner peace from day to day problems,
Godiji Parshwanath Pratima is so powerful, beautiful you don't want to move a step aside from looking it.
The carvings made are such elegant that it seems like Dev Nirmit Derasar.

featured_reviews.name: Ankit Dubey
featured_reviews.review_text: One of the oldest Jain Temple in Mumbai. This Temple is also a show of the extraordinary architecture. The temple looks like an 18th century palace from inside especially at night. The inside of the temple is mostly made of white marble and has magnificent artwork on the walls, pillars and walkways. A different serenity can be found in the temple atmosphere. Calmness and peace of mind is sure to be found when spending time here. This is a must visit place for people who love medivial and ancient architecture as well as old antique buildings. One if the finest made temples in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Bhavik Vasha
featured_reviews.review_text: one of the oldest Jain temples in Mumbai. This temple maintains the sanctity of Jain principles.

featured_reviews.name: vikas mehta
featured_reviews.review_text:
It is a heritage temple with unbelievable carvings on the wall.
You will experience eternal peace while being in the temple .
The temple is more than 200+years old and the idol is more older than it having magical and mysterious powers.

featured_reviews.name: Vini Jain
featured_reviews.review_text: “A truly peaceful and spiritual experience. The Jain Mandir is beautifully maintained, with intricate carvings and a serene atmosphere that instantly brings calmness to the soul. A perfect place for quiet reflection and prayer. The positive energy here is truly unmatched. Highly recommended for anyone seeking inner peace and spiritual connection.”

featured_reviews.name: Jayant
featured_reviews.review_text: This is basically an ancient religious temple on banks of one of the sacred rivers Narmada. Access by road, nearby railway station Khandwa or Indore in Madhya Pradesh. The rituals of Narmada Parikrama (Walking around entire stretch of the river Narmada - originating at Sihawa mountain at the eastern corner of the state to Arebian sea in Gujarat State) mostly begins and ends at this place/temple.  Do not expect Star facilities here but highest devotion and attainment of Moksha.
